checks.comparison: With 0<t(m)<infinity and m,n>0, all positive workloads have positive finite equilibrium time. For S<=m, monotonicity gives t(S)<=t(m), so the real scalar comparison applies after toReal/ofReal transport. The chosen finite minimizer and source branch therefore give Vstar<=2*min B. Against a positive competitor S<=m, Bstar<=B(S)<=2*V(S,rho), yielding factor4. For S>m, the mixture is >=t(m) and the coefficient >=Lminus, hence V(S,rho)>=Lminus*t(m)>=Bstar; the same factor4 holds. The competitor quantifier is genuinely all positive naturals, not restricted to the search range. This compares the displayed analytical time expression, not minimax actual runtime.

optimizedBatch minimizes the outer-min batchObjective over the nonempty finite list 1,...,m; the compiler type identifies the same value with the infimum over Fin m via j.val+1. It does not minimize the bare nonbaseline expression over all positive naturals. ENNReal is linearly ordered even at infinity, so this finite attainment statement needs only m>0, not sign or finite-time premises. In the nonnegative analytic domain, S>=m gives t(S)>=t(m), making the outer-min value Lminus*t(m); thus larger S cannot improve the global outer-min objective.

scalarCoefficient is the source family coefficient times rho*a+(1-rho)*b. For a>=b>0 and positive S, the branch rho=1 has value L*a; the other branch rho=b/a has mixture<=2b and hence value<=2*(L*b+D*sqrt(a*b/S)). For every competitor rho>=1/2 its value is >=L*a/2. For rho<1/2 its L-term is >=L*b/2 and AM-GM gives its D-term >=2*D*(1-rho)*sqrt(a*b/S)>=D*sqrt(a*b/S). These establish B/2<=V for B=min(L*a,L*b+D*sqrt(a*b/S)). Both branch probabilities are legal. This verifies the exact 2 and 1/2 constants independently, including L=0 or D=0.

The source case n<=u=D*sqrt(m)/L<=m with L,D>0 gives u>=1, ceil(u) in 1,...,m and rho=u/m in (0,1]. To verify the concrete factor20, in the positive finite-time case let H=sum_i 1/tau_i. For all positive r, t(r)>=r/H; for r>=n, t(r)<=(r+n)/H. Thus the tuned mixture is <=5*u/H since t(m)<=2*m/H and t(ceil u)<=(u+1+n)/H<=3*u/H. Its coefficient is <=2L, because ceil(u)>=u and D*sqrt(m)/u=L. Any competitor S<=m has V>=B(S)/2>=L*u/(2H), using D*sqrt(m)=L*u<=L*m. Any S>m has V>=L*m/H>=L*u/H. Consequently Vtuned<=20*Vcompetitor. This proves a valid rounded constant-factor interpretation of source Theorem15 case1; no numerical diagnostic is used as evidence. For a zero advertised worker time, every positive-work equilibrium time is zero, so the ratio comparison is 0<=0. If every worker bound is infinity, every positive-work equilibrium time is infinity; the positive smoothness and positive rho make both time coefficients infinity, so the bound is valid. Otherwise H is positive finite, including prefixes containing infinite bounds, and the real argument applies. No finite-latency restriction is silently added to ratio_case_one.
